```{r}
# Completed 300-iteration experiment: calibration, fresh baseline, and policy all use this source.
experiment <- "2026-10-23a-calib-age-1pct-300it-v1.9"
# These folders have different roles: simulation results, analysis code, survey data, and paper files.
scenario_root <- "/Users/jakob/git/public-svn/matsim/scenarios/countries/jp/gunma/gunma-v1.9"
project_root <- "/Users/jakob/git/matsim-gunma"
shared_root <- "/Users/jakob/git/shared-svn/projects/matsim-gunma"
paper_root <- "/Users/jakob/git/PAPER-EWGT"
results_dir <- file.path(scenario_root, "_develop", experiment, "experiments/v1.9/results")
# The map describes the full synthetic population; behavioural results still use the selected run.
map_population_file <- file.path(project_root, "input/v1.8/e05_plans_static-100pct.xml.gz")
map_extractor <- file.path(project_root, "scripts/extract-map-population.py")
map_coordinates_file <- file.path(project_root, "target/paper-ewgt/map-population-100pct.csv.gz")
# PNGs go straight into the paper; CSVs and copyable LaTeX go into a separate experiment folder.
figure_dir <- file.path(paper_root, "figures")
table_dir <- file.path(project_root, "target", "paper-ewgt", experiment)
# Pass the same experiment and destination to the optional Bash download block below.
Sys.setenv(GUNMA_EXPERIMENT = experiment, GUNMA_RESULTS = results_dir)
```

## Optional download

Run the setup above before running this Bash block manually. Rendering never connects to the cluster. The transfer preserves the overall, age, and comparison folders; events, networks, and iteration directories are excluded.

```{bash}
#| eval: false
#| echo: true
: "${GUNMA_EXPERIMENT:?Run the R setup first}"
: "${GUNMA_RESULTS:?Run the R setup first}"
mkdir -p "$GUNMA_RESULTS"
rsync -avm -e "ssh -T -o RemoteCommand=none -o RequestTTY=no" \
  --include='/overall/' --include='/age/' --include='/comparison/' \
  --exclude='/*/' --exclude='ITERS/' \
  --include='*/' \
  --include='selection.json' --include='selected-config.xml' \
  --include='trial-*.xml' --include='*.output_config.xml' \
  --include='*.modestats.csv' --include='*.scorestats.csv' \
  --include='*.output_persons.csv.gz' --include='*.output_trips.csv.gz' \
  --include='*.output_legs.csv.gz' --include='count_comparison_by_hour.csv' \
  --exclude='*' \
  "mc:/net/ils/rehmann/matsim-gunma/$GUNMA_EXPERIMENT/experiments/v1.9/results/" "$GUNMA_RESULTS/"
```

## Inputs and checks

All calibration, baseline, policy, and traffic-count inputs use the completed 300-iteration `experiment`. Both calibration trials are read from their final `selection.json` files. The input inventory records every source path. Survey and boundary files are fixed reference inputs. Missing evidence stops the document before any paper figures are replaced.

```{r}
# Packages: data handling and plotting, spatial boundaries, XML configs, Sankey plots, and panel layouts.
library(tidyverse)
library(sf)
library(xml2)
library(ggalluvial)
library(patchwork)

# 1. Find the selected trial from each calibration stage; do not assume the final trial is the best.
selection_files <- file.path(results_dir, c("overall", "age"), "selection.json")
missing <- selection_files[!file.exists(selection_files)]
if (length(missing)) stop("Missing completed calibration selections; run the download block first:\n",
                          paste(missing, collapse = "\n"))
overall_selection <- jsonlite::fromJSON(selection_files[1])
age_selection <- jsonlite::fromJSON(selection_files[2])
stopifnot(overall_selection$stage == "overall", age_selection$stage == "age")
for (selection in list(overall_selection, age_selection)) {
  completed <- selection$history |> filter(is.finite(mae)) |> arrange(mae, trial)
  stopifnot(nrow(completed) > 0, selection$trial == completed$trial[1],
            near(selection$mae, completed$mae[1]), selection$inputs$iterations == 300)
}
# Keep four datasets separate: overall calibration, age calibration, unrestricted baseline, and policy.
run_dirs <- c(
  overall = file.path(results_dir, "overall", sprintf("run-%03d", overall_selection$trial)),
  age = file.path(results_dir, "age", sprintf("run-%03d", age_selection$trial)),
  baseline = file.path(results_dir, "comparison", "baseline"),
  policy = file.path(results_dir, "comparison", "policy")
)
# 2. Build a file inventory. Requiring exactly one match avoids accidentally mixing two run outputs.
inputs <- tibble(dataset = character(), kind = character(), path = character())
for (dataset in names(run_dirs)) {
  for (kind in c("persons", "trips", "config")) {
    suffix <- if (kind == "config") "xml" else "csv.gz"
    matches <- list.files(run_dirs[[dataset]], full.names = TRUE,
                          pattern = paste0("\\.output_", kind, "\\.", gsub(".", "\\.", suffix, fixed = TRUE), "$"))
    if (length(matches) != 1) stop("Expected one ", kind, " output in ", run_dirs[[dataset]], "; found ", length(matches))
    inputs <- add_row(inputs, dataset = dataset, kind = kind, path = matches)
  }
}
# Trips describe whole journeys; legs are also needed to detect driving within a multimode journey.
policy_legs_file <- list.files(run_dirs[["policy"]], pattern = "\\.output_legs\\.csv\\.gz$", full.names = TRUE)
if (length(policy_legs_file) != 1) stop("Expected one policy legs output in ", run_dirs[["policy"]])
# The road-count comparison is produced by SimWrapper post-processing, not by this R script.
counts_file <- file.path(run_dirs[["baseline"]], "analysis", "traffic-car", "count_comparison_by_hour.csv")
# Survey files and geographic boundaries are fixed references, shared across experiments.
survey_persons_file <- file.path(shared_root, "data/processed/travel_survey/person_attributes.csv")
survey_activities_file <- file.path(shared_root, "data/processed/travel_survey/activities.csv")
target_file <- file.path(project_root, "resources/mode_share_per_group_dist_ref.csv")
distance_target_file <- file.path(project_root, "resources/mode_share_per_dist_ref.csv")
gunma_file <- file.path(shared_root, "data/raw/01_shapefiles/gunma_2450/gunma_2450.shp")
japan_file <- file.path(shared_root, "data/raw/01_shapefiles/zzz_deprecated/jp_administrative_boundaries/gadm41_JPN_1.shp")
age_config_file <- file.path(results_dir, "age", sprintf("trial-%03d.xml", age_selection$trial))
overall_config_file <- file.path(results_dir, "overall", sprintf("trial-%03d.xml", overall_selection$trial))
# Stop early if an input is missing, including the companion files needed to read each shapefile.
required <- c(map_population_file, map_extractor, inputs$path, policy_legs_file, counts_file, survey_persons_file, survey_activities_file,
              target_file, distance_target_file, age_config_file, overall_config_file,
              sub("\\.shp$", ".shx", c(gunma_file, japan_file)),
              sub("\\.shp$", ".dbf", c(gunma_file, japan_file)),
              sub("\\.shp$", ".prj", c(gunma_file, japan_file)), gunma_file, japan_file)
missing <- required[!file.exists(required)]
if (length(missing)) stop("Missing required inputs; no paper figures have been replaced:\n", paste(missing, collapse = "\n"))

# 3. Define a common set of modes, age groups, and colours so every figure is comparable.
modes <- c("car", "ride", "bike", "walk")
age_groups <- c("0-17", "18-29", "30-44", "45-64", "65-74", "75-84", "85+")
age_breaks <- c(0, 18, 30, 45, 65, 75, 85, Inf)
mode_cols <- c(car = "#0072B2", ride = "#009E73", walk = "#E69F00", bike = "#D55E00")
# Explicit boundaries: 17/18, 29/30, 44/45, 64/65, 74/75, and 84/85.
stopifnot(identical(as.character(cut(c(0,17,18,29,30,44,45,64,65,74,75,84,85,100),
  age_breaks, right = FALSE, labels = age_groups)), rep(age_groups, each = 2)))

# 4. Read each dataset into named lists: e.g. persons$baseline and trips$policy.
# Exclude inbound commuters only from resident behaviour analyses, not from the map or road counts.
persons <- list(); trips <- list(); configs <- list()
for (dataset in names(run_dirs)) {
  persons[[dataset]] <- read_delim(inputs$path[inputs$dataset == dataset & inputs$kind == "persons"],
    delim = ";", show_col_types = FALSE) |> filter(!str_starts(person, "commuter"))
  stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(persons[[dataset]]$person),
            !anyNA(persons[[dataset]][c("age", "sex", "home_x", "home_y")]),
            all(persons[[dataset]]$sex %in% c("m", "f")))
  # right = FALSE makes the boundaries inclusive at the lower age: age 75 belongs to 75-84.
  persons[[dataset]] <- persons[[dataset]] |>
    mutate(age_group = cut(age, age_breaks, right = FALSE, labels = age_groups),
           sex = factor(sex, c("m", "f"), c("Male", "Female")))
  stopifnot(!anyNA(persons[[dataset]]$age_group))
  trips[[dataset]] <- read_delim(inputs$path[inputs$dataset == dataset & inputs$kind == "trips"],
    delim = ";", show_col_types = FALSE) |> filter(!str_starts(person, "commuter"))
  stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(trips[[dataset]][c("person", "trip_number")]),
            all(trips[[dataset]]$person %in% persons[[dataset]]$person),
            all(trips[[dataset]]$main_mode %in% modes))
  configs[[dataset]] <- read_xml(inputs$path[inputs$dataset == dataset & inputs$kind == "config"], options = "NONET")
}
# Demographic and home attributes must match for a paired policy comparison.
base_population <- persons$baseline |> select(person, age, sex, home_x, home_y) |> arrange(person)
policy_population <- persons$policy |> select(person, age, sex, home_x, home_y) |> arrange(person)
stopifnot(identical(base_population, policy_population))
# A score comparison is only meaningful here if both cases use exactly the same scoring parameters.
for (module in c("scoring", "advancedScoring")) {
  base_scoring <- xml_find_first(configs$baseline, paste0("/config/module[@name='", module, "']"))
  policy_scoring <- xml_find_first(configs$policy, paste0("/config/module[@name='", module, "']"))
  stopifnot(!inherits(base_scoring, "xml_missing"), !inherits(policy_scoring, "xml_missing"),
            identical(as.character(base_scoring), as.character(policy_scoring)))
}
# The fresh baseline must retain the selected age-calibration scoring parameters.
for (module in c("scoring", "advancedScoring")) {
  stopifnot(identical(as.character(xml_find_first(configs$age, paste0("/config/module[@name='", module, "']"))),
                      as.character(xml_find_first(configs$baseline, paste0("/config/module[@name='", module, "']")))))
}
# Check matched case settings and completion from effective configs and final mode statistics.
run_settings <- tibble()
for (dataset in names(run_dirs)) {
  settings <- xml_find_all(configs[[dataset]], "/config/module/param[@name='lastIteration' or @name='randomSeed' or @name='flowCapacityFactor' or @name='storageCapacityFactor']")
  run_settings <- bind_rows(run_settings, tibble(dataset, module = xml_find_chr(settings, "string(../@name)"),
    parameter = xml_attr(settings, "name"), value = xml_attr(settings, "value")))
  stats_file <- list.files(run_dirs[[dataset]], pattern = "\\.modestats\\.csv$", full.names = TRUE)
  stopifnot(length(stats_file) == 1)
  stats <- read_delim(stats_file, show_col_types = FALSE)
  last_iteration <- as.numeric(run_settings$value[run_settings$dataset == dataset & run_settings$parameter == "lastIteration"])
  stopifnot(length(last_iteration) == 1, last_iteration == 300, max(stats$iteration) == last_iteration)
}
stopifnot(identical(run_settings |> filter(dataset == "baseline") |> select(-dataset),
                    run_settings |> filter(dataset == "policy") |> select(-dataset)))
# 5. Check the policy itself: residents aged 75+ must have no driving trips or car legs.
policy_legs <- read_delim(policy_legs_file, delim = ";", show_col_types = FALSE)
restricted <- persons$policy |> filter(age >= 75) |> select(person)
driving_check <- tibble(
  check = c("Restricted residents", "Restricted residents' driving trips", "Restricted residents' driving legs"),
  n = c(nrow(restricted),
        sum(trips$policy$person %in% restricted$person &
          (trips$policy$main_mode == "car" | str_detect(trips$policy$modes, "(^|-)car(-|$)"))),
        sum(policy_legs$person %in% restricted$person & policy_legs$mode == "car"))
)
if (any(driving_check$n[-1] > 0)) stop("Policy integrity failure: restricted residents still drive. Trips: ",
  driving_check$n[2], "; legs: ", driving_check$n[3])

# 6. Reconstruct the survey comparison independently of the simulated results.
# Preserve IDs as text; keep non-travellers in the persons table, even though they have no trips.
survey_persons <- read_csv(survey_persons_file, col_types = cols(idx = col_character()), show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  transmute(person = idx, age, sex = factor(gender, c("m", "f"), c("Male", "Female")),
            age_group = cut(age, age_breaks, right = FALSE, labels = age_groups))
# Each activity after the initial home activity has an incoming trip. Keep the four modelled modes.
survey_trips <- read_csv(survey_activities_file, col_types = cols(p_id = col_character()), show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  filter(act_num > 0, leg_mode %in% modes, leg_dist >= 0) |>
  transmute(person = p_id, main_mode = leg_mode, traveled_distance = leg_dist)
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(survey_persons$person), !anyNA(survey_persons[c("age_group", "sex")]),
          all(survey_trips$person %in% survey_persons$person))
# Use the original survey target for distance comparison, preserving its distance definition.
distance_target <- read_csv(distance_target_file, show_col_types = FALSE)
# Sum the distance-specific target contributions to obtain a modal share for each age group.
# Renormalising makes the four shares add to one within each age group.
age_target <- read_csv(target_file, show_col_types = FALSE) |> filter(age != "", !is.na(age)) |>
  mutate(age_group = str_replace_all(age, " ", "")) |>
  group_by(age_group, main_mode) |> summarise(share = sum(share), .groups = "drop") |>
  group_by(age_group) |> mutate(share = share / sum(share)) |> ungroup()
stopifnot(setequal(age_target$age_group, age_groups), setequal(age_target$main_mode, modes))

# Selected overall constants and age adjustments are read from the actual trial XMLs.
age_xml <- read_xml(age_config_file, options = "NONET")
overall_xml <- read_xml(overall_config_file, options = "NONET")
# The scoring module holds overall mode constants; select the default resident scoring group.
asc_modes <- xml_find_all(age_xml, "/config/module[@name='scoring']/parameterset[@type='scoringParameters'][not(param[@name='subpopulation']) or param[@name='subpopulation']/@value='null']/parameterset[@type='modeParams']")
overall_asc <- tibble(mode = xml_attr(xml_find_first(asc_modes, "param[@name='mode']"), "value"),
  overall = as.numeric(xml_attr(xml_find_first(asc_modes, "param[@name='constant']"), "value"))) |> filter(mode %in% modes)
# The age calibration should retain the overall constants selected in the first stage.
selected_modes <- xml_find_all(overall_xml, "/config/module[@name='scoring']/parameterset[@type='scoringParameters'][not(param[@name='subpopulation']) or param[@name='subpopulation']/@value='null']/parameterset[@type='modeParams']")
selected_overall <- tibble(mode = xml_attr(xml_find_first(selected_modes, "param[@name='mode']"), "value"),
  overall = as.numeric(xml_attr(xml_find_first(selected_modes, "param[@name='constant']"), "value"))) |> filter(mode %in% modes)
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(arrange(overall_asc, mode), arrange(selected_overall, mode))))
# The advancedScoring module holds deltaConstant: an additive correction for each age and mode.
age_adjustments <- tibble()
for (group in xml_find_all(age_xml, "/config/module[@name='advancedScoring']/parameterset[@type='scoringParameters']")) {
  age <- xml_attr(xml_find_first(group, "param[@name='age_group']"), "value")
  nodes <- xml_find_all(group, "parameterset[@type='modeParams']")
  age_adjustments <- bind_rows(age_adjustments, tibble(age_group = age,
    mode = xml_attr(xml_find_first(nodes, "param[@name='mode']"), "value"),
    adjustment = as.numeric(xml_attr(xml_find_first(nodes, "param[@name='deltaConstant']"), "value"))))
}
# Effective ASC = overall ASC + age adjustment. Seven age groups x four modes gives 28 values.
asc_values <- age_adjustments |> left_join(overall_asc, by = "mode") |>
  mutate(effective = overall + adjustment, age_group = factor(age_group, age_groups)) |>
  arrange(age_group, match(mode, modes))
stopifnot(nrow(asc_values) == 28, !anyDuplicated(asc_values[c("age_group", "mode")]),
          setequal(asc_values$mode, modes), !anyNA(asc_values),
          all(is.finite(asc_values$effective)), all(asc_values$adjustment[asc_values$mode == "walk"] == 0),
          overall_asc$overall[overall_asc$mode == "walk"] == 0,
          all(abs(asc_values$effective - asc_values$overall - asc_values$adjustment) < 1e-12))
# The selected age output must use the exported calibration parameters.
base_mode_nodes <- xml_find_all(configs$age, "/config/module[@name='scoring']/parameterset[@type='scoringParameters'][not(param[@name='subpopulation']) or param[@name='subpopulation']/@value='null']/parameterset[@type='modeParams']")
base_mode_values <- tibble(mode = xml_attr(xml_find_first(base_mode_nodes, "param[@name='mode']"), "value"),
  overall = as.numeric(xml_attr(xml_find_first(base_mode_nodes, "param[@name='constant']"), "value"))) |> filter(mode %in% modes)
base_adjustments <- tibble()
for (group in xml_find_all(configs$age, "/config/module[@name='advancedScoring']/parameterset[@type='scoringParameters']")) {
  nodes <- xml_find_all(group, "parameterset[@type='modeParams']")
  base_adjustments <- bind_rows(base_adjustments, tibble(
    age_group = xml_attr(xml_find_first(group, "param[@name='age_group']"), "value"),
    mode = xml_attr(xml_find_first(nodes, "param[@name='mode']"), "value"),
    adjustment = as.numeric(xml_attr(xml_find_first(nodes, "param[@name='deltaConstant']"), "value"))))
}
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(arrange(base_mode_values, mode), arrange(overall_asc, mode))),
          isTRUE(all.equal(arrange(base_adjustments, age_group, mode), arrange(age_adjustments, age_group, mode))))

# Prepare plot data once; no objects from another notebook are needed.
# 7. Calculate reusable summaries for all figures. Here p means persons and t means trips.
shares <- tibble(); trip_rates <- tibble()
for (dataset in c("Survey", "overall", "age", "baseline", "policy")) {
  p <- if (dataset == "Survey") survey_persons else persons[[dataset]]
  t <- if (dataset == "Survey") survey_trips else trips[[dataset]]
  # Start from all persons and attach their trip counts; absent counts become zero.
  # This keeps the trips-per-resident denominator from excluding people who stayed at home.
  rates <- p |> select(person, age_group, sex) |> left_join(count(t, person, name = "n_trips"), by = "person") |>
    mutate(n_trips = replace_na(n_trips, 0L))
  stopifnot(nrow(rates) == nrow(p), sum(rates$n_trips) == nrow(t))
  trip_rates <- bind_rows(trip_rates, rates |> group_by(age_group, sex) |>
    summarise(trips_per_resident = mean(n_trips), residents = n(), .groups = "drop") |> mutate(dataset = dataset))
  # Attach age and sex to each trip, count modes, and fill unused modes with zero.
  # Modal shares use trips as the denominator; they are not shares of people.
  shares <- bind_rows(shares, t |> left_join(select(p, person, age_group, sex), by = "person") |>
    count(age_group, sex, main_mode) |>
    complete(age_group, sex, main_mode = modes, fill = list(n = 0)) |>
    group_by(age_group, sex) |> mutate(share = n / sum(n)) |> ungroup() |> mutate(dataset = dataset))
}
shares <- shares |> mutate(main_mode = factor(main_mode, c("car", "ride", "walk", "bike")))
stopifnot(all(shares |> group_by(dataset, age_group, sex) |> summarise(total = sum(share), .groups = "drop") |> pull(total) |> near(1)))
# 8. Pair the same person and trip number across cases to identify actual mode transitions.
# Unmatched trips are counted separately below rather than silently treated as mode switches.
matched_trips <- inner_join(trips$baseline |> select(person, trip_number, mode_base = main_mode),
  trips$policy |> select(person, trip_number, mode_policy = main_mode), by = c("person", "trip_number")) |>
  left_join(select(persons$baseline, person, age_group, age, sex), by = "person")
matching <- tibble(check = c("Unmatched baseline trips", "Unmatched policy trips", "Matched trips", "Matched residents"),
  n = c(nrow(anti_join(trips$baseline, trips$policy, by = c("person", "trip_number"))),
        nrow(anti_join(trips$policy, trips$baseline, by = c("person", "trip_number"))),
        nrow(matched_trips), nrow(base_population)))
if (any(matching$n[1:2] > 0)) warning("Unmatched trips: Figure 8 uses matched trips only; see the matching table.")
# Pair scores by person, then calculate policy minus baseline. Negative values indicate a lower score.
score_pairs <- persons$baseline |> select(person, age_group, sex, score_base = executed_score) |>
  left_join(persons$policy |> select(person, score_policy = executed_score), by = "person") |>
  mutate(score_change = score_policy - score_base)
stopifnot(all(is.finite(score_pairs$score_change)))
# Road-count input includes all simulated traffic. SimWrapper has already expanded the 1% sample.
# Sum hourly volumes for each link to obtain the daily values used in the scatter plot.
counts <- read_csv(counts_file, show_col_types = FALSE)
stopifnot(all(c("link_id", "observed_traffic_volume", "simulated_traffic_volume") %in% names(counts)),
          all(is.finite(counts$observed_traffic_volume)), all(is.finite(counts$simulated_traffic_volume)),
          all(counts$observed_traffic_volume >= 0), all(counts$simulated_traffic_volume >= 0))
daily_counts <- counts |> group_by(link_id) |>
  summarise(observed = sum(observed_traffic_volume), simulated = sum(simulated_traffic_volume), .groups = "drop")

# Calculate both MAEs from the same resident trips used in the calibration figures.
model_age_fit <- shares |> filter(dataset %in% c("overall", "age", "baseline")) |>
  group_by(dataset, age_group, main_mode) |> summarise(n = sum(n), .groups = "drop") |>
  group_by(dataset, age_group) |> mutate(share = n / sum(n)) |> ungroup() |>
  left_join(age_target |> rename(reference_share = share), by = c("age_group", "main_mode")) |>
  group_by(dataset) |> summarise(age_mae_pp = 100 * mean(abs(share - reference_share)), .groups = "drop")
stopifnot(near(age_selection$mae, model_age_fit$age_mae_pp[model_age_fit$dataset == "age"] / 100))
aggregate_shares <- shares |> filter(dataset %in% c("Survey", "overall", "age", "baseline")) |>
  group_by(dataset, main_mode) |> summarise(n = sum(n), .groups = "drop") |>
  group_by(dataset) |> mutate(share = n / sum(n)) |> ungroup()
aggregate_fit <- aggregate_shares |> filter(dataset != "Survey") |>
  left_join(aggregate_shares |> filter(dataset == "Survey") |>
    select(main_mode, reference_share = share), by = "main_mode") |>
  group_by(dataset) |> summarise(aggregate_mae_pp = 100 * mean(abs(share - reference_share)), .groups = "drop")
fit_summary <- left_join(model_age_fit, aggregate_fit, by = "dataset")
stopifnot(!anyNA(fit_summary), all(is.finite(fit_summary$age_mae_pp)))

# All inputs and numerical checks above pass before creating exports.
dir.create(figure_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create(table_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
# Show the run choices, fit errors, input paths, and checks in the HTML report.
# Multiply share errors by 100 to express them in percentage points (0.01 becomes 1 pp).
knitr::kable(tibble(experiment, overall_trial = overall_selection$trial, age_trial = age_selection$trial,
                    overall_MAE_pp = 100 * overall_selection$mae, age_MAE_pp = 100 * age_selection$mae), digits = 3)
knitr::kable(inputs)
knitr::kable(fit_summary, digits = 3)
write_csv(fit_summary, file.path(table_dir, "calibration-fit-summary.csv"))
write_csv(aggregate_shares, file.path(table_dir, "calibration-aggregate-shares.csv"))
write_csv(tibble(dataset = names(run_dirs), path = unname(run_dirs)), file.path(table_dir, "selected-runs.csv"))
knitr::kable(tibble(reference = c("Survey persons", "Survey activities", "Age targets", "Distance targets", "Traffic counts", "Gunma boundaries", "Japan boundaries"),
                   path = c(survey_persons_file, survey_activities_file, target_file, distance_target_file, counts_file, gunma_file, japan_file)))
knitr::kable(run_settings)
knitr::kable(driving_check)
knitr::kable(matching)
# Keep machine-readable versions of the checks alongside the paper tables.
write_csv(inputs, file.path(table_dir, "simulation-inputs.csv"))
write_csv(matching, file.path(table_dir, "matching.csv"))
write_csv(driving_check, file.path(table_dir, "driving-check.csv"))
```

## Figure 1 — Study area and 100% synthetic population

The map shows home locations for the **100% synthetic population**, including inbound commuters, from the population-generation input. It is not a 100% simulation result. All behavioural figures still use the selected 1% experiment. The main view focuses on Gunma Prefecture and its immediate surroundings; a small inset locates Gunma among Japan's main islands.

```{r}
# Read the map boundaries. EPSG:2450 uses metres; EPSG:4326 uses longitude and latitude.
gunma <- st_read(gunma_file, quiet = TRUE) |> st_transform(2450)
japan <- st_read(japan_file, quiet = TRUE) |> st_transform(4326)
# Extract only home coordinates, streaming the full XML; reuse the cache while its source is unchanged.
if (!file.exists(map_coordinates_file) ||
    file.mtime(map_coordinates_file) < max(file.mtime(map_population_file), file.mtime(map_extractor))) {
  status <- system2("python3", c(shQuote(map_extractor), "--input", shQuote(map_population_file),
                                "--output", shQuote(map_coordinates_file)))
  if (status != 0) stop("Could not extract the full map population from ", map_population_file)
}
# The compact cache contains one row per person in the full population, including commuters.
map_persons <- read_csv(map_coordinates_file, col_types = cols(person = col_character()), show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  mutate(population = if_else(str_starts(person, "commuter"), "Inbound commuters", "Gunma residents"))
stopifnot(!anyNA(map_persons[c("person", "home_x", "home_y")]), !anyDuplicated(map_persons$person),
          all(is.finite(map_persons$home_x)), all(is.finite(map_persons$home_y)),
          all(c("Gunma residents", "Inbound commuters") %in% map_persons$population))
knitr::kable(count(map_persons, population, name = "persons"))
cat("Map population source:", map_population_file)
# Coordinates already use EPSG:2450; geom_point avoids millions of separate sf geometries.
homes <- map_persons |> select(home_x, home_y, population)
# Crop to Gunma and a small surrounding buffer; distant commuter homes remain in the input.
main_xlim <- c(st_bbox(gunma)[["xmin"]] - 8000, st_bbox(gunma)[["xmax"]] + 8000)
main_ylim <- c(st_bbox(gunma)[["ymin"]] - 6000, st_bbox(gunma)[["ymax"]] + 6000)
# Draw residents first, then commuters and the prefecture outline.
# Small, transparent dots limit overplotting; commuters use a larger dot so they remain visible.
map_main <- ggplot() + geom_sf(data = japan |> st_transform(2450), fill = "grey97", colour = "grey80", linewidth = 0.2) +
  geom_point(data = filter(homes, population == "Gunma residents"), aes(home_x, home_y, colour = population),
             size = 0.06, alpha = 0.16, stroke = 0) +
  geom_point(data = filter(homes, population == "Inbound commuters"), aes(home_x, home_y, colour = population),
             size = 0.11, alpha = 0.35, stroke = 0) +
  geom_sf(data = gunma, fill = NA, colour = "#0072B2", linewidth = 0.6) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("Gunma residents" = "#333333", "Inbound commuters" = "#D55E00")) +
  coord_sf(xlim = main_xlim, ylim = main_ylim, datum = NA) +
  theme_void(base_size = 20) + labs(colour = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", plot.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0)) + guides(colour = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size = 2, alpha = 1)))
# The inset shows the main Japanese islands; exclude the distant southern and offshore islands.
# Place labels on the main map, leaving the inset as a simple locator.
map_inset <- ggplot() + geom_sf(data = japan, fill = "grey94", colour = "grey65", linewidth = 0.15) +
  geom_sf(data = gunma |> st_transform(4326), fill = "#0072B2", colour = "#0072B2", linewidth = 0.2) +
  coord_sf(xlim = c(129, 146), ylim = c(31, 46), datum = NA) + theme_void() +
  theme(plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = "grey80", linewidth = 0.3),
        plot.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0))
# Keep the enlarged locator inside the main map panel, including when the paper crops its margins.
figure_1 <- map_main +
  inset_element(map_inset, left = 0.01, bottom = 0.57, right = 0.33, top = 0.99, align_to = "panel")
figure_1
# Save the named plot at publication resolution; width and height are in inches.
ggsave(file.path(figure_dir, "map_gunma_population.png"), figure_1, width = 6.8, height = 5.5, dpi = 300, bg = "white")
write_csv(count(map_persons, population, name = "persons"), file.path(table_dir, "map-population-counts.csv"))
```

## Figure 2 — Model V1, Model V2, and Reference by age

Reference is the pooled age-specific survey target; Model V1 is the selected overall-only calibration; Model V2 is the selected age-calibration run. Iteration settings for each run are reported above. This compares fit to calibration targets, not independent validation. Sexes are pooled using trip counts.

```{r}
# Pool male and female trip counts before calculating shares; do not average their percentages.
# V1 is the selected overall-only run; V2 is the selected age-calibration run.
calibration_shares <- shares |> filter(dataset %in% c("overall", "age")) |>
  group_by(dataset, age_group, main_mode) |> summarise(n = sum(n), .groups = "drop") |>
  group_by(dataset, age_group) |> mutate(share = n / sum(n)) |> ungroup() |>
  mutate(dataset = recode(dataset, overall = "Model V1", age = "Model V2")) |>
  bind_rows(age_target |> mutate(dataset = "Reference")) |>
  mutate(age_group = factor(age_group, age_groups),
         main_mode = factor(main_mode, c("car", "ride", "walk", "bike")),
         dataset = factor(dataset, c("Model V1", "Model V2", "Reference")))
stopifnot(all(calibration_shares |> group_by(age_group, dataset) |>
  summarise(total = sum(share), .groups = "drop") |> pull(total) |> near(1)))
# Each age panel contains three stacked bars, ordered V1, V2, then Reference.
# The separate text layer adds one label per bar rather than one label per coloured segment.
# Fix stacking order explicitly, including when replotting from the exported CSV.
figure_2 <- ggplot(calibration_shares |>
  mutate(main_mode = factor(main_mode, levels = c("car", "ride", "walk", "bike"))),
  aes(dataset, share, fill = main_mode)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.85, position = position_stack(reverse = TRUE)) +
  facet_grid(. ~ age_group, switch = "x") +
  geom_text(data = distinct(calibration_shares, age_group, dataset), inherit.aes = FALSE,
    aes(x = dataset, y = 0.02, label = dataset),
    colour = "white", angle = 90, hjust = 0, size = 7) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = mode_cols, breaks = c("car", "ride", "walk", "bike"), guide = guide_legend(reverse = FALSE)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_percent()) + coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 1)) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 24) + labs(x = "Age group", y = "Modal split (trip-based)", fill = "Mode") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_blank(), axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(), panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        strip.background = element_blank(), strip.placement = "outside", legend.position = "bottom")
figure_2
ggsave(file.path(figure_dir, "calibration_age_comparison.png"), figure_2, width = 12, height = 6, dpi = 300, bg = "white")
write_csv(calibration_shares, file.path(table_dir, "calibration-age-comparison.csv"))
# Paper fit comparison: equal weight for each of the seven age groups and four modes.
# Use the same selected age trial as the plotted V2.
calibration_errors <- calibration_shares |>
  filter(dataset != "Reference") |>
  left_join(calibration_shares |> filter(dataset == "Reference") |>
              select(age_group, main_mode, reference_share = share),
            by = c("age_group", "main_mode")) |>
  mutate(absolute_error_pp = 100 * abs(share - reference_share))
stopifnot(nrow(calibration_errors) == 56,
          !anyNA(calibration_errors$absolute_error_pp))
calibration_fit <- calibration_errors |>
  group_by(dataset) |>
  summarise(mae_percentage_points = mean(absolute_error_pp), .groups = "drop")
calibration_fit
write_csv(calibration_fit, file.path(table_dir, "calibration-age-fit.csv"))
```

### Traffic-count statistics for the manuscript

These statistics use one daily total per matched directional link, with equal weight per link. Relative error is `(simulated - observed) / observed`. Links with zero observed daily volume are reported separately and excluded from relative-error and SQV summaries.

```{r}
# Calculate errors from daily totals, not from an average of hourly percentage errors.
# SQV uses MATSim's daily car-count scale of 10,000; the hourly scale of 1,000 is not appropriate here.
count_validation_daily <- daily_counts |>
  mutate(relative_error = if_else(observed > 0, (simulated - observed) / observed, NA_real_),
         daily_sqv = if_else(observed > 0,
           1 / (1 + sqrt((simulated - observed)^2 / (10000 * observed))), NA_real_))
valid_count_links <- count_validation_daily |> filter(observed > 0)
if (!nrow(valid_count_links)) stop("No links with positive observed daily traffic are available for validation.")

# Include exactly +/-20% and +/-40% in the respective bands.
# A tiny tolerance avoids classifying a boundary differently because of floating-point rounding.
count_validation <- valid_count_links |> summarise(
  compared_links = n(),
  within_20_percent = 100 * mean(abs(relative_error) <= 0.20 + 1e-12),
  within_40_percent = 100 * mean(abs(relative_error) <= 0.40 + 1e-12),
  below_minus_20_percent = 100 * mean(relative_error < -0.20 - 1e-12),
  above_plus_20_percent = 100 * mean(relative_error > 0.20 + 1e-12),
  mean_absolute_relative_error_percent = 100 * mean(abs(relative_error)),
  mean_daily_sqv = mean(daily_sqv)
) |> mutate(excluded_zero_observed_links = sum(count_validation_daily$observed == 0))
stopifnot(near(count_validation$within_20_percent + count_validation$below_minus_20_percent +
                count_validation$above_plus_20_percent, 100),
          count_validation$within_40_percent >= count_validation$within_20_percent,
          all(between(valid_count_links$daily_sqv, 0, 1)))

# Present both the denominator and all six statistics quoted in the paper.
count_validation_table <- tibble(
  Statistic = c("Compared directional links", "Excluded links with zero observed volume",
                "Within +/-20%", "Within +/-40%", "Relative error below -20%", "Relative error above +20%",
                "Mean absolute relative error", "Mean daily link-level SQV"),
  Value = c(count_validation$compared_links, count_validation$excluded_zero_observed_links,
            count_validation$within_20_percent, count_validation$within_40_percent,
            count_validation$below_minus_20_percent, count_validation$above_plus_20_percent,
            count_validation$mean_absolute_relative_error_percent, count_validation$mean_daily_sqv),
  Unit = c("links", "links", rep("%", 5), "0-1")
)
knitr::kable(count_validation_table, digits = 2)
# Preserve full precision and per-link values so the rounded manuscript numbers can be checked.
write_csv(count_validation, file.path(table_dir, "traffic-count-validation-summary.csv"))
write_csv(count_validation_daily, file.path(table_dir, "traffic-count-validation-by-link.csv"))
```

Daily SQV is calculated as $1/(1+\sqrt{(S-O)^2/(10{,}000\,O)})$, where $S$ and $O$ are daily simulated and observed volumes. The reported value is the arithmetic mean across links, consistent with MATSim's `CountComparisonAnalysis`; it is not an average of the hourly SQV column. The 0.75 and 0.80 thresholds discussed in the manuscript are context for interpretation, not automatic acceptance criteria here.

Copyable LaTeX with the **current experiment's** values (rather than the previous manuscript's numbers):

```{r}
#| results: asis
# Use whole percentages for the bands, one decimal for MARE, and two decimals for SQV.
# The percentages below are based on positive-observation links; excluded zeros are shown above.
count_validation_text <- sprintf(paste0(
  "We compared simulated daily link volumes against real-world traffic counts obtained from JARTIC ",
  "\\citep{zotero-item-3922} and MLIT \\citep{mlit_2023}, using %d matched directional links. ",
  "For %.0f\\%% of links, simulated volumes were within $\\pm$20\\%% of observed volumes; ",
  "for %.0f\\%%, they were within $\\pm$40\\%%. ",
  "Relative errors were below $-$0.20 for %.0f\\%% of links and above 0.20 for %.0f\\%%. ",
  "The mean absolute relative error was %.1f\\%%.\n\n",
  "The mean daily link-level Scalable Quality Value (SQV) was %.2f."),
  count_validation$compared_links, count_validation$within_20_percent, count_validation$within_40_percent,
  count_validation$below_minus_20_percent, count_validation$above_plus_20_percent,
  count_validation$mean_absolute_relative_error_percent, count_validation$mean_daily_sqv)
cat("\n```latex\n", count_validation_text, "\n```\n", sep = "")
writeLines(count_validation_text, file.path(table_dir, "traffic-count-validation-text.tex"))
```

## Figure 4 — Modal shares by distance: Model V2 and Reference

```{r}
# Distance values are in metres; the displayed group labels are in kilometres.
distance_breaks <- c(0, 1000, 2000, 5000, 10000, 20000, Inf)
distance_labels <- c("<1", "1–2", "2–5", "5–10", "10–20", "20+")
# Within each distance band, divide each mode count by the total number of trips in that band.
base_distance <- trips$age |> mutate(distance_group = cut(traveled_distance, distance_breaks,
  right = FALSE, labels = distance_labels)) |> count(distance_group, main_mode) |>
  complete(distance_group, main_mode = modes, fill = list(n = 0)) |> group_by(distance_group) |>
  mutate(share = n / sum(n)) |> ungroup() |> mutate(dataset = "Model V2")
# Give survey and model distance bands the same labels and ordering before combining them.
ref_distance <- distance_target |> mutate(distance_group = factor(dist_group,
  levels = c("0 - 1000", "1000 - 2000", "2000 - 5000", "5000 - 10000", "10000 - 20000", "20000+"), labels = distance_labels), dataset = "Reference")
distance_shares <- bind_rows(ref_distance, base_distance) |>
  mutate(dataset = factor(dataset, c("Model V2", "Reference")), main_mode = factor(main_mode, c("car", "ride", "walk", "bike")))
figure_4 <- ggplot(distance_shares, aes(dataset, share, fill = main_mode)) +
  geom_col(position = position_stack(reverse = TRUE), width = 0.85) +

    colour = "white", angle = 90, hjust = 0, size = 7) +

  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_percent()) + theme_minimal(base_size = 24) +
  labs(x = "Trip distance (km)", y = "Modal split (trip-based)", fill = "Mode") +
```

```{r}
  count(mode_base, mode_policy, name = "n_trips")

  geom_alluvium(aes(fill = mode_base), alpha = 0.7, width = 0.25, reverse = FALSE) +
  geom_stratum(aes(fill = after_stat(stratum)), width = 0.25, reverse = FALSE) +
```

## Copyable LaTeX ASC rows

Paste the overall row followed by the seven **adjustment** rows into the existing seven-column scoring table. Effective constants equal the overall constant plus the age adjustment; walk remains zero. The compact check table below contains effective constants, not adjustments.

```{r}
#| results: asis
# Rearrange the adjustment data into one row per age group and one column per mode.
asc_wide <- asc_values |> select(age_group, mode, adjustment) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = mode, values_from = adjustment) |> arrange(age_group)
overall_wide <- overall_asc |> pivot_wider(names_from = mode, values_from = overall)
# Build rows in the existing scoring table order: description, symbol, car, ride, bike, walk, source.
# The overall row and adjustment rows must be added together to obtain the effective age-specific ASC.
latex_rows <- sprintf("Overall ASC (util) & $C_m$ & %.3f & %.3f & %.3f & %.3f & Calibration \\\\",
                      overall_wide$car, overall_wide$ride, overall_wide$bike, overall_wide$walk)
for (i in seq_len(nrow(asc_wide))) {
  age_label <- gsub("-", "--", as.character(asc_wide$age_group[i]), fixed = TRUE)
  latex_rows <- c(latex_rows, sprintf("Age adjustment: %s & $\\Delta C_{a,m}$ & %.3f & %.3f & %.3f & %.3f & Calibration \\\\",
    age_label, asc_wide$car[i], asc_wide$ride[i], asc_wide$bike[i], asc_wide$walk[i]))
}
# Print a copyable LaTeX code block in the HTML; this does not create a full table environment.
cat("\n```latex\n", paste(latex_rows, collapse = "\n"), "\n```\n", sep = "")
# Produce a separate check table of effective constants; these are not the adjustment rows.
effective_table <- asc_values |> select(age_group, mode, effective) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = mode, values_from = effective) |> select(age_group, all_of(modes))
effective_display <- effective_table
for (mode in modes) effective_display[[mode]] <- sprintf("%.3f", effective_display[[mode]])
effective_latex <- knitr::kable(effective_display, format = "latex", align = "lrrrr", row.names = FALSE,
                              col.names = c("Age group", "Car", "Ride", "Bike", "Walk"))
cat("\n```latex\n", effective_latex, "\n```\n", sep = "")
# Export paste-ready LaTeX and full-precision CSV values for later checking or reuse.
writeLines(latex_rows, file.path(table_dir, "asc-scoring-table-rows.tex"))
writeLines(effective_latex, file.path(table_dir, "asc-effective-check.tex"))
write_csv(asc_values, file.path(table_dir, "asc-values.csv"))
write_csv(overall_asc, file.path(table_dir, "asc-overall.csv"))
```

## Inventory and within-run stability

The final 50 iterations are compared with the preceding 50. A mode-share mean shift below 1 percentage point is a screening aid, not a convergence certificate. Score changes are reported in utils and are compared **within** each run; scores across trials are not directly comparable because ASCs change. The mode-history files describe the full simulated population, whereas the age-specific calculations below exclude inbound commuters, as in the paper.

```{r}
#| eval: false
library(tidyverse)
library(xml2)
checkpoint_results <- "/Users/jakob/git/public-svn/matsim/scenarios/countries/jp/gunma/gunma-v1.9/_develop/2026-10-23a-calib-age-1pct-300it-v1.9/experiments/v1.9/results"
checkpoint_output <- "/Users/jakob/git/matsim-gunma/target/paper-ewgt/checkpoint-300it"
dir.create(checkpoint_output, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
checkpoint_modes <- c("car", "ride", "walk", "bike")
checkpoint_ages <- c("0-17", "18-29", "30-44", "45-64", "65-74", "75-84", "85+")
checkpoint_expected <- 300L
checkpoint_window <- 50L
checkpoint_one <- function(folder, pattern) {
  paths <- list.files(folder, pattern = pattern, full.names = TRUE)
  if (length(paths) == 1L) paths else NA_character_
}
checkpoint_read_stats <- function(path) {
  if (is.na(path)) return(tibble())
  # A snapshot of a running file can contain an unfinished final row.
  read_delim(path, delim = ";", col_types = cols(.default = col_double()),
             show_col_types = FALSE, progress = FALSE) |>
    filter(is.finite(iteration)) |> arrange(iteration) |> distinct(iteration, .keep_all = TRUE)
}
checkpoint_folders <- c(
  list.dirs(file.path(checkpoint_results, "age"), recursive = FALSE, full.names = TRUE),
  file.path(checkpoint_results, "comparison", c("baseline", "policy")))
checkpoint_folders <- checkpoint_folders[dir.exists(checkpoint_folders) &
  grepl("(run-[0-9]+|baseline|policy)$", checkpoint_folders)]
if (!length(checkpoint_folders)) stop("No run snapshots found. Execute the download block first.")
checkpoint_inventory <- tibble(folder = checkpoint_folders) |>
  mutate(run = basename(folder), stage = basename(dirname(folder)),
         config = map_chr(folder, checkpoint_one, "\\.output_config\\.xml$"),
         mode_file = map_chr(folder, checkpoint_one, "\\.modestats\\.csv$"),
         score_file = map_chr(folder, checkpoint_one, "\\.scorestats\\.csv$"),
         persons_file = map_chr(folder, checkpoint_one, "\\.output_persons\\.csv\\.gz$"),
         trips_file = map_chr(folder, checkpoint_one, "\\.output_trips\\.csv\\.gz$"),
         mode_history = map(mode_file, checkpoint_read_stats),
         score_history = map(score_file, checkpoint_read_stats),
         last_iteration = map_int(mode_history, ~ if (nrow(.x)) as.integer(max(.x$iteration)) else NA_integer_),
         expected_iteration = map_int(config, function(path) {
           if (is.na(path)) return(checkpoint_expected)
           as.integer(xml_attr(xml_find_first(read_xml(path, options = "NONET"),
             "/config/module[@name='controller']/param[@name='lastIteration']"), "value"))
         }),
         finished = !is.na(last_iteration) & last_iteration >= expected_iteration,
         fit_ready = finished & !is.na(persons_file) & !is.na(trips_file),
         input_plans = map_chr(config, function(path) {
           if (is.na(path)) return(NA_character_)
           xml_attr(xml_find_first(read_xml(path, options = "NONET"),
             "/config/module[@name='plans']/param[@name='inputPlansFile']"), "value")
         })) |> arrange(stage, run)
checkpoint_inventory |> select(stage, run, last_iteration, expected_iteration, finished, fit_ready, input_plans)

checkpoint_mode_history <- map2_dfr(checkpoint_inventory$mode_history,
  paste(checkpoint_inventory$stage, checkpoint_inventory$run, sep = "/"), function(x, run_id) {
    if (!nrow(x)) return(tibble())
    x |> pivot_longer(any_of(checkpoint_modes), names_to = "mode", values_to = "share") |>
      filter(is.finite(share)) |> mutate(run_id = run_id)
  })
checkpoint_drift <- checkpoint_mode_history |> group_by(run_id, mode) |>
  group_modify(~ {
    # Require the full windows; a running trial may not have reached them yet.
    end <- max(.x$iteration)
    late <- filter(.x, iteration > end - checkpoint_window)
    prior <- filter(.x, iteration > end - 2 * checkpoint_window, iteration <= end - checkpoint_window)
    enough <- nrow(late) == checkpoint_window && nrow(prior) == checkpoint_window
    tibble(last_iteration = end, full_windows = enough,
      last_mean_percent = 100 * mean(late$share),
      drift_pp = if (enough) 100 * (mean(late$share) - mean(prior$share)) else NA_real_,
      last_range_pp = 100 * diff(range(late$share)))
  }) |> ungroup()
checkpoint_drift
checkpoint_stability_plot <- ggplot(checkpoint_mode_history, aes(iteration, 100 * share, colour = mode)) +
  geom_line() + facet_wrap(~run_id, ncol = 3) + theme_minimal() +
  labs(x = "Iteration within run", y = "Full-population modal share (%)", colour = "Mode")
checkpoint_stability_plot
checkpoint_score_history <- map2_dfr(checkpoint_inventory$score_history,
  paste(checkpoint_inventory$stage, checkpoint_inventory$run, sep = "/"), function(x, run_id) {
    if (!nrow(x) || !"avg_executed" %in% names(x)) return(tibble())
    x |> filter(is.finite(avg_executed)) |> mutate(run_id = run_id)
  })
if (nrow(checkpoint_score_history)) {
  print(ggplot(checkpoint_score_history, aes(iteration, avg_executed)) + geom_line() +
    facet_wrap(~run_id, scales = "free_y", ncol = 3) + theme_minimal() +
    labs(x = "Iteration within run", y = "Mean executed score (utils)"))
}
write_csv(checkpoint_inventory |> select(-mode_history, -score_history), file.path(checkpoint_output, "inventory.csv"))
write_csv(checkpoint_drift, file.path(checkpoint_output, "mode-drift.csv"))
ggsave(file.path(checkpoint_output, "within-run-modal-stability.png"), checkpoint_stability_plot,
       width = 12, height = max(5, 2.5 * ceiling(n_distinct(checkpoint_mode_history$run_id) / 3)), dpi = 150)
```

## Age fit, aggregate fit, and the previous 50-iteration discrepancy

The age target is the same survey target used above. Aggregate shares are trip-weighted; the age MAE gives each of the 28 group–mode combinations equal weight. The “perfect age fit” column shows the aggregate implied by the target shares **using that run's age distribution of trips**, separating demographic weights from remaining within-age errors. An incomplete run is not interpreted as a finished calibration result.

```{r}
#| eval: false
checkpoint_target <- read_csv("/Users/jakob/git/matsim-gunma/resources/mode_share_per_group_dist_ref.csv",
  show_col_types = FALSE) |> filter(!is.na(age), age != "") |>
  mutate(age_group = str_replace_all(age, " ", "")) |>
  group_by(age_group, main_mode) |> summarise(target = sum(share), .groups = "drop") |>
  group_by(age_group) |> mutate(target = target / sum(target)) |> ungroup()
checkpoint_get_shares <- function(persons_file, trips_file, run_id) {
  tryCatch({
    p <- read_delim(persons_file, delim = ";", show_col_types = FALSE, progress = FALSE) |>
      filter(!str_starts(person, "commuter")) |>
      transmute(person, age_group = as.character(cut(age, c(0, 18, 30, 45, 65, 75, 85, Inf),
                                                    right = FALSE, labels = checkpoint_ages)))
    t <- read_delim(trips_file, delim = ";", show_col_types = FALSE, progress = FALSE) |>
      filter(!str_starts(person, "commuter"))
    stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(p$person), all(t$person %in% p$person),
              all(t$main_mode %in% checkpoint_modes), !anyNA(p$age_group))
    t |> left_join(p, by = "person") |> count(age_group, main_mode) |>
      complete(age_group = checkpoint_ages, main_mode = checkpoint_modes, fill = list(n = 0)) |>
      group_by(age_group) |> mutate(age_trips = sum(n), share = n / age_trips) |> ungroup() |>
      mutate(run_id = run_id)
  }, error = function(e) {
    warning("Skipping incomplete/unreadable snapshot ", run_id, ": ", conditionMessage(e))
    tibble()
  })
}
checkpoint_ready <- checkpoint_inventory |> filter(fit_ready)
checkpoint_shares <- pmap_dfr(checkpoint_ready |> select(persons_file, trips_file) |>
  mutate(run_id = paste(checkpoint_ready$stage, checkpoint_ready$run, sep = "/")), checkpoint_get_shares)
if (!nrow(checkpoint_shares)) {
  message("No completed person/trip snapshots yet. Inspect the running histories above and download again later.")
} else {
  checkpoint_errors <- checkpoint_shares |> left_join(checkpoint_target, by = c("age_group", "main_mode"))
  stopifnot(!anyNA(checkpoint_errors$share), !anyNA(checkpoint_errors$target))
  checkpoint_fit <- checkpoint_errors |> group_by(run_id) |>
    summarise(age_mae_pp = 100 * mean(abs(share - target)), .groups = "drop")
  print(checkpoint_fit)
  print(ggplot(checkpoint_fit |> filter(str_starts(run_id, "age/")), aes(run_id, age_mae_pp)) +
    geom_point() + geom_line(aes(group = 1)) + theme_minimal() +
    labs(x = "Completed age-calibration trial", y = "Age-specific MAE (percentage points)") +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)))
  checkpoint_aggregate <- checkpoint_errors |> group_by(run_id) |>
    mutate(total_trips = sum(n)) |> group_by(run_id, main_mode) |>
    summarise(simulated_percent = 100 * sum(n) / first(total_trips),
      perfect_age_fit_percent = 100 * sum(age_trips * target) / first(total_trips), .groups = "drop")
  print(checkpoint_aggregate)
  # Use the selected trial, or the provisional best completed trial during calibration.
  age_fit <- checkpoint_fit |> filter(str_starts(run_id, "age/")) |> arrange(age_mae_pp, run_id)
  selection_path <- file.path(checkpoint_results, "age", "selection.json")
  candidate <- if (file.exists(selection_path)) {
    sprintf("age/run-%03d", jsonlite::fromJSON(selection_path)$trial)
  } else if (nrow(age_fit)) age_fit$run_id[1] else NA_character_
  if (!is.na(candidate) && "comparison/baseline" %in% checkpoint_fit$run_id &&
      candidate %in% checkpoint_fit$run_id) {
    config_for <- function(id) checkpoint_inventory$config[
      paste(checkpoint_inventory$stage, checkpoint_inventory$run, sep = "/") == id]
    scoring_signature <- function(path) {
      nodes <- xml_find_all(read_xml(path, options = "NONET"),
        "/config/module[@name='scoring' or @name='advancedScoring']")
      stopifnot(length(nodes) == 2)
      gsub(">[[:space:]]+<", "><", as.character(nodes))
    }
    same_scoring <- identical(scoring_signature(config_for(candidate)),
                              scoring_signature(config_for("comparison/baseline")))
    print(tibble(candidate, selected = file.exists(selection_path), same_scoring,
      baseline_minus_candidate_age_mae_pp =
        checkpoint_fit$age_mae_pp[checkpoint_fit$run_id == "comparison/baseline"] -
        checkpoint_fit$age_mae_pp[checkpoint_fit$run_id == candidate]))
    if (!same_scoring) warning("Candidate and baseline scoring differ; this is not a pure starting-plan/convergence comparison.")
  } else message("Fresh-start baseline comparison pending; warm-started trials alone cannot resolve the earlier discrepancy.")
  checkpoint_age_weights <- checkpoint_shares |> distinct(run_id, age_group, age_trips) |>
    group_by(run_id) |> mutate(trip_weight_percent = 100 * age_trips / sum(age_trips)) |> ungroup()
  print(checkpoint_age_weights)
  checkpoint_age_plot <- checkpoint_errors |> pivot_longer(c(share, target), names_to = "source", values_to = "value") |>
    ggplot(aes(age_group, 100 * value, colour = source, group = source)) + geom_point() + geom_line() +
    facet_grid(run_id ~ main_mode) + theme_minimal() +
    labs(x = "Age group", y = "Resident trip modal share (%)", colour = NULL) +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
  print(checkpoint_age_plot)
  write_csv(checkpoint_fit, file.path(checkpoint_output, "age-fit.csv"))
  write_csv(checkpoint_aggregate, file.path(checkpoint_output, "aggregate-fit.csv"))
  write_csv(checkpoint_age_weights, file.path(checkpoint_output, "age-trip-weights.csv"))
}
```

**How to read the checkpoint:** Falling age MAE and flat late-iteration mode/score histories are promising evidence. Successive trials use different parameters, so agreement between their outputs alone does not establish convergence. The previous selected 50-iteration age trial had MAE 0.46 pp, but the separately restarted policy baseline had MAE 3.34 pp; they had identical scoring parameters and different starting plans. Once the new `comparison/baseline` is available, compare its age MAE and aggregate shares with the selected age trial, confirm matching scoring parameters, and inspect their input-plan paths in the inventory. Until then, this checkpoint **cannot establish that the fresh-start discrepancy is resolved**, even if run-007 looks stable. Do not substitute a calibration trial for the paired policy baseline when calculating policy effects.
